page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics are relatively weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 905.0 and poor single-threaded compression speeds. However, the 12 dedicated physical cores deliver average multi-core performance, as demonstrated by a Passmark CPU score of 10042.2 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4589.0. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 56.47 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, though the Passmark memory score is weak. The instance handles Redis SET operations at an average rate of 8.35 million operations per second, but static web serving throughput is weak at 5.98 GB/sec.

Given the hardware profile and benchmark results, the ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is best suited for multi-threaded workloads that do not require high single-core clock speeds or local storage. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and basic multi-threaded data processing. It can also handle small-scale language model inference, processing 115.95 text generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, though performance drops significantly on larger models. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a balanced resource density for legacy enterprise applications and general-purpose utility computing where dedicated CPU allocation is required without the premium of high-frequency processors.
